question.leadin: This nation's troops were committed to Iraq by John Howard's government.
question.text: Name this former British penal colony with capital at Canberra. Prior to Iraq and Afghanistan, its most notable post-World War II overseas troop deployment came as peacekeepers in East Timor.
question.clue: One criminal from this country fashioned his own suit of armor and got besieged at Glenrowan.

swap.text: This man has hidden in an Ecuadorian embassy since 2012, a saga stemming from sexual assault charges now dropped. His 2010 talk was "Why the World Needs Wikileaks".
swap.clue: Daniel Ellsberg praised this man, saying his actions were similar to Ellsberg's handling of the Pentagon Papers.

question.text: This is the collective name given to Aboriginals who were taken from their families and forced to assimilate into white society. In 2008, Prime Minister Kevin Rudd formally apologized to this group.
question.clue: An official 2007 apology to these people and their descendants was made by then-Prime Minister Kevin Rudd.

swap.leadin: In order to pass otherwise deadlocked legislation, this party called its country's only-ever joint sitting of Parliament in 1974.
swap.text: Name this party. Australia's 1975 constitutional crisis was caused by John Kerr's dismissal of a Prime Minister of this party, Gough Whitlam, after the Liberal-National Coalition blocked supply to this left-wing party's government.
swap.clue: This political party passed important social reforms under leaders like Bob Hawke and Gough Whitlam.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the only successful armed uprising in Australian history.
question.text: Major George Johnston invaded Government House and placed Bligh under arrest in this capital city of New South Wales.
question.clue: This city is the largest to be served by the Snowy Mountains Hydroelectric Scheme, whose construction caused its country to ease pro-white immigration policies.

swap.leadin: To support his country's involvement in one conflict, this leader stated he was "all the way with LBJ."
swap.text: Name this Australian prime minister who disappeared in 1967 while swimming at Cheviot Beach.
swap.clue: This prime minister declared that he was "all the way with LBJ" in showing his country's support for the Vietnam War.

question.leadin: Identify the following about penal colonies.
question.text: The First Fleet, under the command of Arthur Phillip, established a prison colony in this Australian state. Sydney is located in this present-day state.
question.clue: The Tenterfield Oration, calling for states to unify for purposes of defense, was given in this state, which was also the landing spot for Arthur Phillip and the First Fleet.

swap.leadin: Doris Pilkington's Follow the Rabbit-Proof Fence discusses the escape of three of these people to Jigalong in Western Australia.
swap.text: The Moore River settlement that was depicted in the book housed these natives of Australia. Children of these people were forcibly taken to settlements such as Doomadgee Mission and Ebenezer Mission for "re-education."
swap.clue: Many of these people were taken from their families and integrated into white culture, becoming the Stolen Generation.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the "White Australia" policy of discrimination.
question.text: This Australian prime minister began dismantling White Australia in 1966, a year before his mysterious disappearance during a swimming incident while in office.
question.clue: Liashchenko proposed that the White-Russian epic folk hero Solovei Budomirovich is based on a historical king by this name, who had married the daughter of Yaroslav the Wise, Elizabeth, only after achieving fame through his Byzantine adventures.

swap.leadin: During World War II, the US 1st Marine Division adopted this ballad by Banjo Paterson as their official march.
swap.text: Name this song, which "the Band Played" in an Eric Bogle song memorializing the Gallipoli campaign. It is considered Australia's "unofficial national anthem."
swap.clue: While at an outback station, Banjo Paterson wrote this "unofficial Australian anthem" which describes a "jolly swagman camped by a billabong." This song's title refers to the motion of a "tucker bag" containing a "jumbuck."

question.leadin: Identify some things about the geography of Australia.
question.text: This tallest mountain in Australia takes its name from a similar peak in Poland, which is named after a Polish hero of the American Revolutionary War.

swap.leadin: The Bringing Them Home report described abuses that these people faced as part of a "relocalisation" program.
swap.text: Name these people, who were the subject of a "National Sorry Day" introduced in 2008. The Stolen Generations were children of these people that were taken away from their parents.
swap.answerHtml: Aboriginal Australians [accept Aborigines or Aboriginals; accept answers describing Indigenous or native Australians; prompt on Australians]
swap.clue: That report documented a policy of taking children of these people and bringing them up in white culture.

question.text: This holiday is celebrated on April 25, the first day of the Gallipoli landings. Dawn services featuring the Ode of Remembrance often take place on this holiday, which is named for a corps that fought at Gallipoli.
question.clue: Their most notable action is remembered in the song titled "And the Band Played" a certain nationalist folk tune, was supported by the French from Kum Kale, and was advocated by Winston Churchill.

swap.leadin: A key controversy in the history wars is over whether the separation of families from children described by this adjective constitutes genocide.
swap.text: Give the adjective commonly used to describe those "generations" of children, the subjects of the report Bringing Them Home.

question.text: This town in the Outback is situated at the geographical center of Australia. It is named after the wife of telegrapher Sir Charles Todd.

swap.text: This World War II-era Prime Minister of Australia served for a record 18 years. After an electoral defeat, he formed the Liberal Party to provide conservative opposition to the Labor Party.
swap.clue: This Liberal politician who also tried to ingratiate himself with ordinary citizens by delivering the 'Forgotten People' Speech. He was succeeded by Harold Holt.

question.leadin: This man names the iron bar correcting for vertical magnetism in calibrating compass binnacles, but he is better known for a journey on which he was accompanied by the adorable cat Trim.
question.text: Name this English cartographer who became the first man to circumnavigate Australia and identify it as a continent.
question.clue: This explorer was a member of William Bligh's Second Breadfruit Voyage that successfully brought the crop to the Caribbean.

swap.text: Lindqvist recounted the mistreatment of Aboriginal Australians in a 2007 book titled for this phrase. This two-word Latin phrase names a legal doctrine used to justify colonization that was rejected by the Mabo case.
swap.answerHtml: terra nullius [accept terrae nullius; accept Terra Nullius: A Journey Through No One’s Land]

question.leadin: Answer the following about Australia's relations with Papua New Guinea.
question.text: After defeating Somare in a 2011-2012 constitutional crisis, Prime Minister Peter O'Neill allowed Kevin Rudd to reopen this site in Papua New Guinea. However, the Papuan Supreme Court ruled that this Australian immigrant detention camp was in fact illegal, and O'Neill closed it in 2017.

swap.leadin: Name these locations that appear in the Holmes canon.
swap.text: In "The Boscombe Valley Mystery," the last words of Charles McCarthy are interpreted by Holmes to refer to the name of this city. This boomtown of the Australian gold rush was the site of the Eureka Stockade.
